claim: ATT&CK is the common language for attacker behaviour
quote: The MITRE ATT&CK framework [89] has emerged as the de facto standard for structuring TTPs from CTI reports, offering a comprehensive knowledge base and ontology of adversarial tactics and techniques from real-world observations that are widely recognized by the cybersecurity community. Such a knowledge base provides security professionals with a common language for understanding, categorizing, and mitigating cyber threats.
issue: 'de facto standard' plus 'a common language' carries 'the common language'; Buchel's scope is CTI, which is the dissertation's context here.

claim: On the 50 most common techniques, the best systems reach 80% precision at 66% recall
quote: even when considering only the top-50 most common TTPs, the best-performing solutions reach a precision of around 80% for a recall of around 66%
locator: Sec. 1 key insights, p. 4622 printed (PDF p. 3); Table 12 (TRAM2, Generation: 80.00 / 66.30), Sec. 7
issue: 'around' dropped, but Table 12 gives 80.00 % and 66.30 %, so the figures are exact. These are closed-set results on TRAM2 (the most favourable setting); open-set is worse, so the omission understates rather than overstates the unreliability.

claim: Even identifying which techniques a report describes is not yet reliable
quote: for less common TTPs, performances quickly drop (esp. for precision, going way below 40% in realistic settings)
locator: Sec. 1 key insights, p. 4622 printed (PDF p. 3)
issue: Buchel evaluates TTP extraction, not ordering; the sentence correctly claims only identification.
